issues.legal_issue: A purchaser seeking specific performance must establish readiness and willingness through evidence competent to prove the purchaser’s own knowledge and capacity to perform.
material_facts: The purchaser did not enter the witness box to testify about readiness and willingness or the ability to pay the balance of the price.
The purchaser’s power-of-attorney holder was appointed after the relevant events and lacked personal knowledge of them.
Apart from an assertion in the plaint, no evidence was led to establish readiness and willingness or capacity to perform.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser failed to establish readiness and willingness, and was not entitled to discretionary specific performance.
issues.legal_principle: Under Janki Vashdeo Bhojwani v. Indusind Bank Ltd., a power-of-attorney holder may testify about acts performed by that holder but cannot testify for the principal about the principal’s acts or matters within the principal’s personal knowledge. Under Vidhyadhar v. Manikrao, a party’s failure to testify and submit to cross-examination may support an adverse presumption that the party’s case is incorrect. Applying those principles, the absence of competent evidence of readiness and willingness meant the purchaser had not established entitlement to discretionary specific performance.

rule.if: specific_performance_proceeding and purchaser_did_not_testify_personally and agent_lacked_personal_knowledge and no_independent_readiness_evidence

predicates.specific_performance_proceeding: The proceeding seeks specific performance of a sale agreement.
predicates.purchaser_did_not_testify_personally: The purchaser did not testify about the purchaser’s own readiness, willingness, or ability to perform.
predicates.agent_lacked_personal_knowledge: The purchaser’s agent lacked personal knowledge of the relevant events or matters personal to the purchaser.
predicates.no_independent_readiness_evidence: No other evidence was presented to support the purchaser’s readiness and willingness to perform.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance proceeding involves a purchaser who does not testify personally, whose agent lacks personal knowledge, and who presents no other evidence of readiness and willingness, readiness and willingness are not established.

issues.legal_issue: A purchaser cannot maintain a claim for specific performance based on a cancelled sale agreement without challenging the cancellation.
material_facts: The seller cancelled the agreement after giving notice and informed the purchaser of the cancellation.
The purchaser did not challenge the communication cancelling the agreement.
The purchaser sought specific performance without seeking a declaration that the cancellation was invalid.
issues.conclusion: The claim for specific performance based on the cancelled agreement, without a challenge to the cancellation, was not maintainable.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on I.S. Sikandar (D) by L.Rs. v. K. Subramani, which held that a claim for specific performance based on a terminated agreement is not maintainable when the plaintiff has not sought a declaration that the termination is invalid.

predicates.specific_performance_proceeding: The proceeding seeks specific performance of a sale agreement.
predicates.seller_cancelled_agreement: The seller communicated cancellation of the sale agreement to the purchaser.
predicates.purchaser_did_not_challenge_cancellation: The purchaser did not seek relief challenging the cancellation of the agreement.

issues.definition: When specific performance is sought after the seller has communicated cancellation and the purchaser has not challenged that cancellation, the claim based on the cancelled agreement is not maintainable.

issues.legal_issue: A seller gives due intimation of mortgage release when the sale agreement requires notice and the seller notifies the purchaser of the release and provides the release document.
material_facts: The agreement required the seller to notify the purchaser after obtaining release of the property from mortgage.
After the mortgage was redeemed, the seller notified the purchaser by registered post and provided a photocopy of the release deed.
The purchaser disputed receiving the release document and sought a no-dues certificate.
issues.conclusion: The seller gave due intimation of the release, and the contrary finding that the seller had not given due intimation was unsustainable.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the notice requirement in the parties’ agreement and found that the seller’s notification of the mortgage release, together with the photocopy of the release deed, constituted due intimation. No earlier case or statutory provision was relied on for this conclusion.

rule.if: mortgage_contingent_sale_dispute and contract_required_notice_of_release and seller_notified_purchaser_of_release and seller_provided_release_document

predicates.mortgage_contingent_sale_dispute: The dispute concerns a sale agreement under which performance follows release of the property from mortgage.
predicates.contract_required_notice_of_release: The agreement required the seller to notify the purchaser after the property was released from mortgage.
predicates.seller_notified_purchaser_of_release: The seller sent the purchaser notice that the property had been released from mortgage.
predicates.seller_provided_release_document: The seller provided the purchaser with a document evidencing release of the property from mortgage.

issues.definition: In a dispute about a mortgage-contingent sale agreement, when the agreement requires notice and the seller notifies the purchaser of the release and provides a document evidencing it, due intimation of release is given.
